A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AETHER study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between appendix sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original depth-estimation, camera-pose, video-prediction, and visual-planning results in Tables 1–6, including a depth-objective ablation.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds reconstruction runtime measurements in Table 7 and qualitative comparisons in Figures 5–7.

M1.justification: Equation (3) corrects the specified disparity input transform from (2x_disp − 1)/max(x_disp) to 2x_disp/max(x_disp) − 1, matching the existing normalization description. The architecture, conditioning, training objectives, and inference procedures otherwise remain unchanged; an implementation change or retraining is not established.

E1.justification: The reconstruction benchmarks, prediction/planning tasks, and synthetic in-domain/out-of-domain coverage remain unchanged. Appendix H identifies previously unspecified training-game sources; the additional qualitative examples do not establish a distinct new dataset, task, or evaluation domain.

E2.justification: Figure 5 adds CUT3R comparisons for reconstruction examples previously shown only for AETHER. Table 7 adds a runtime comparison against DUSt3R-GA, MASt3R-GA, and MonST3R-GA. These methods already appeared in reconstruction benchmarks, whose comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix I introduces reconstruction throughput evaluation on an A100, reporting FPS at 144 × 512 for the three baselines and 480 × 640 for AETHER. The original benchmark protocols, metrics, validation sample counts, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds qualitative evidence for the existing depth-removal ablation; its quantitative results in Tables 5–6 are unchanged. Figures 5–6 add reconstruction comparisons and planning examples. Appendix B explains annotation safeguards but does not report a new robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v3's discussion of annotation uncertainty is qualitative and does not introduce statistical estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain identical results. New Table 7 reports 6.14 FPS for AETHER versus 0.76, 0.31, and 0.35 FPS for DUSt3R-GA, MASt3R-GA, and MonST3R-GA, respectively, at the differing resolutions specified there. Figures 5–7 add qualitative outputs and comparisons rather than demonstrating a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: Equation (3) makes a mathematically non-equivalent correction: normalization now precedes multiplication by two and subtraction of one, consistent with the stated mapping to [−1, 1]. The remaining mathematical formulation, camera-conversion algorithm, and appendix loss definitions are retained; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows reconstruction superiority from 'far exceeds' specialist models to 'comparable with or even better than' them. It also replaces the autonomous-trajectory-planning formulation with camera-trajectory-conditioned prediction and visual planning. The central unified reconstruction, prediction, and planning contribution remains intact.

C2.justification: Appendices G–H add explanations involving diffusion priors, image quality, motion blur, synthetic-to-real domain gaps, and imperfect annotations for weaker BONN and ScanNet performance. Appendix B adds robustness reasoning and an unquantified claim that filtering leaves virtually no failure cases. The original conclusion's limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 discloses Cyberpunk2077 and Horizon5 as training sources, approximately 12.5 million raw frames and 8.9 million retained frames, and additional prompt-selection and sequence-rejection details. Appendix C adds a direct code-repository link. These are documentation additions, without evidence that the original training collection or pipeline was replaced.

R1.justification: The reference list and Section 6 related-work discussion are unchanged. The existing positioning around unified world modeling, reconstruction, video generation, and synthetic-data precedents is retained.

P1.justification: v3 locally revises the abstract, expands the author/affiliation block, adds acknowledgments, and introduces supplementary explanatory sections. Existing appendices B–D become C–E with substantially unchanged content, and the main narrative undergoes little rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual presentation of evidence: Figure 5 develops the original teaser scenes into multi-view comparisons with CUT3R, Figure 6 displays planning sequences and geometry, and Figure 7 visualizes the depth ablation. Table 7 adds a runtime display. The original figures and six results tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision and transparency by correcting Equation (3), moderating the abstract to better reflect the mixed reconstruction results, and documenting training-data provenance, filtering, and scale. Added comparative and ablation visualizations make the evidence easier to inspect. The gain remains limited: core quantitative results are unchanged, the new runtime comparison uses different resolutions, and the stronger annotation-robustness assertion lacks quantified validation.
